p5Review.interpretation: P5 is firing frequently, the underlying causes are heterogeneous, and no single engine or operator defect explains all four pauses. The recurring pause is driven by the BASE RATE of unusable institution roots in the frame rather than by one mechanism.

The question of whether a five-item window with a two-item low-yield trigger is the right instrument for this population is DEFERRED to a future governance/methodology revision after this bounded acquisition work.

whyASeparateFactoryAndNotAWiderBootstrap.theOneLineFixRefused: adding the trailing-slash form to forRobotsTxtBootstrap would have been three characters
whyASeparateFactoryAndNotAWiderBootstrap.whyRefused: site-policy discovery would then have TWO admissible starting points, and a caller could decide on its own authority to begin discovery at the trailing-slash form on a host that never redirected there - the caller-manufactured-capability failure mode robotsAuthority.ts exists to prevent, arriving by a different door

theTwoActs.bootstrap: where may policy discovery START? Path set: the canonical policy path
theTwoActs.redirectContinuation: where may a host's own 3xx SEND it? Path set: the canonical policy path or that path with one trailing slash

whyASeparateFactoryAndNotAWiderBootstrap.trustDistinctionIsMechanicallyProvable: from WHICH factory a call site names, not from a comment about intent. Each factory enforces its own path set, and executeWebAttempt verifies scopedToUrl byte-for-byte before any DNS lookup

standardsPosition.fact: RFC 9309 s2.3.1.2 permits robots policy retrieval through redirects, recommends following at least five 'even across authorities', and requires the rules be followed in the context of the INITIAL authority
standardsPosition.whyThatMatters: the RFC names one resource path and does not enumerate admissible redirect TARGETS at all. This repository is deliberately stricter, so every admissible target shape is a LOCAL decision taken one at a time
standardsPosition.thisIsNotClaimedAsRfcRequired: it is a local interoperability decision inside the broader RFC redirect posture, about one observed real-world shape
repositoryRemainsStricterThanTheRfc: same registrable domain only, never across authorities
two admissible target paths, never an arbitrary redirected path

fetchPolicyVersion.whyANewVersion: from byte-identical live evidence v7 can issue a SECOND site-policy request where v6 issued none. A v6 row reading ROBOTS_UNREADABLE after such a 301 means 'this build would not have continued'; the same row stamped v7 would mean 'this build examined the target and refused it for some other reason'. Only the version string can tell those apart
fetchPolicyVersion.migrationCheckedNotAssumed: migration 0007 constrains fetch_policy_version only as <> '' AND length(...) <= 64 on both orgunit_research_runs and orgunit_fetch_observations. Verified against the live PostgreSQL 16 pg_constraint catalogue before the version was changed. 'orgunit-fetch-policy-v7' is 23 characters
fetchPolicyVersion.supersededRunsCannotBeResumed: assertRunIsExecutable refuses a run whose recorded version this build does not implement. Pinned by test for all six superseded versions, v6 included
fetchPolicyVersion.otherPolicyValuesChanged: none. A comment-stripped, whitespace-normalised comparison of policy.ts against v6 differs only in the version assignment, asserted by test

hopBoundArgument.adr0012StructuralArgument: proved a two-request ceiling independently of the constant, because the host was fixed and the only admissible target from an https policy URL was the identical URL that the self-redirect condition refuses
hopBoundArgument.adr0016VoidsWhatRemainedOnASingleOrigin: with the trailing-slash form admissible, canonical -> trailing-slash -> canonical is expressible on one origin
hopBoundArgument.consequence: MAX_ROBOTS_REDIRECT_CONTINUATION_HOPS is now the WHOLE chain bound. Sufficient at 1 - one hop cannot cycle - but raising it would require a visited-URL set
